# Shipping the RED-2.0 admin app to both stores, from Windows, today

## The answer

You can start today and you never strictly need a Mac. Apple's own enrollment page states "No specific device is required to enroll" ([developer.apple.com/support/enrollment](https://developer.apple.com/support/enrollment/)), EAS Build compiles iOS on Expo's cloud macOS VMs ("you don't need a Mac on your local machine", [docs.expo.dev/build-reference/ios-builds](https://docs.expo.dev/build-reference/ios-builds/)), EAS manages the distribution certificate and provisioning profile server-side with no local Keychain ([docs.expo.dev/app-signing/managed-credentials](https://docs.expo.dev/app-signing/managed-credentials/)), and "EAS Submit works on macOS, Linux, and Windows, so you don't need a Mac to ship iOS builds" ([docs.expo.dev/submit/ios](https://docs.expo.dev/submit/ios/)). What you cannot do without hardware is *see the app*: no Mac means no Simulator, so until the iPhone lands your iOS feedback loop is builds and logs, not pixels. `apps/mobile` can live inside this pnpm+Turborepo workspace without abandoning the isolated linker — since SDK 54 "Expo supports isolated dependencies… pnpm using this as the default installation strategy" ([docs.expo.dev/guides/monorepos](https://docs.expo.dev/guides/monorepos/)). Tenancy resolves after login from membership rows, in **one neutral iBookit binary**, because Apple 4.3(a) explicitly names "submitting a separate map app for every city in the world" as the thing not to do while 4.2.6 blesses "a single binary to host all client content in an aggregated or 'picker' model" ([developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/)). Two things this research did **not** answer: the code-reuse audit and data-access shape (subagent 4 returned a null result — see §4), and therefore any credible dev-day sizing for the rebuild.

## 1. The Mac / iPhone line, drawn properly

**Doable today, on Windows, with zero Apple hardware:**

| Step | Source |
|---|---|
| Apple Developer Program enrollment, $99/yr individual ($299/yr Enterprise Program) | [developer.apple.com/support/enrollment](https://developer.apple.com/support/enrollment/) — "No specific device is required to enroll" |
| Enrollment in a browser | Apple: "Enrollment… is available through the Apple Developer app **and on the web**" ([help/account/membership/enrolling-in-the-app](https://developer.apple.com/help/account/membership/enrolling-in-the-app/)) — the web-only path is *inferred*, corroborated only by forum reporting of a "Continue on the web" option |
| Cert + provisioning profile generation | EAS stores them "on EAS servers"; the build VM makes a temporary keychain, imports the cert, places the profile ([docs.expo.dev/app-signing/managed-credentials](https://docs.expo.dev/app-signing/managed-credentials/)) |
| Compiling the `.ipa` | "Create[s] a new macOS VM for the build" with Xcode/Fastlane preinstalled ([docs.expo.dev/build-reference/ios-builds](https://docs.expo.dev/build-reference/ios-builds/)) |
| Submitting to App Store Connect | EAS Submit, explicitly Windows-supported; non-interactive via App Store Connect API Key in `eas.json` ([docs.expo.dev/submit/ios](https://docs.expo.dev/submit/ios/)) |
| TestFlight setup, App Store Connect config (*inferred*) | Browser only. Apple's TestFlight page states no Mac/device requirement on the developer side, but that is absence-of-evidence, not an Apple statement that none is needed. Internal testing = up to 100 team members, **no Beta App Review** ([developer.apple.com/testflight](https://developer.apple.com/testflight/)) |
| APNs push key | `eas credentials` generates it; needs the paid account, not a Mac ([docs.expo.dev/push-notifications/push-notifications-setup](https://docs.expo.dev/push-notifications/push-notifications-setup/)) |

**Impossible without a *Mac*:** local Xcode compiles, running the iOS Simulator, cabled on-device debugging.

**Without an *iPhone* (and no Mac):** you cannot run or look at the app on hardware you control — there is no Simulator to fall back on. The one possible substitute is a browser-based real-device farm (§2), but **nobody verified whether a farm can install an ad-hoc / dev-client `.ipa`** rather than only a TestFlight/production build, so treat that as unproven, not as an escape hatch.

Also: external TestFlight beyond setup is gated on Beta App Review ("your builds are automatically sent for review once they're added to a group", up to 10,000 testers, [developer.apple.com/testflight](https://developer.apple.com/testflight/)); Apple publishes no numeric turnaround for it (gap — the commonly cited 24–48h was **not** verified against an Apple source).

### ⚠️ The one risk that could break the "start today" premise
Subagent 1 flags this as the highest-risk unverified fact in the whole brief and it is a genuine **contradiction between two Apple pages**:
- Apple's enrollment page: no device required.
- Apple's identity-verification page (per search synthesis, **direct fetch failed — unverified**): "you'll need an iPhone or iPad with Touch ID, Face ID, or a passcode enabled, or a Mac with the T2 Security Chip" for certain flows, with the examples given being Account Holder transfer and Enterprise Program — *not clearly* baseline individual enrollment ([developer.apple.com/help/account/membership/identity-verification](https://developer.apple.com/help/account/membership/identity-verification/)).

Do not treat "no device needed to enroll" as settled. **Action on day 1: attempt enrollment and find out.** If it demands biometrics, everything slides until the iPhone arrives.

### Organization vs individual
Individual: your legal personal name is the public App Store seller, and an alias "will cause a delay in the approval"; confirmation normally within 24h of purchase. Organization: needs a legal entity (no DBAs), a **D-U-N-S Number** (not required for government orgs), legal binding authority, a work email on the org domain, and a live website on that domain ([developer.apple.com/support/enrollment](https://developer.apple.com/support/enrollment/)). Apple publishes no timeline for org verification (gap). For a solo dev shipping a B2B platform under someone else's brand, "seller = your legal name" is a real product decision, not a formality.

### The day-to-day loop
Expo Go is instant but limited to Expo-compatible libraries; a **development build** is "your own version of Expo Go where you are free to use any native libraries" and keeps fast refresh after the first native compile — you only rebuild natively for new native deps, native config, or an SDK bump ([docs.expo.dev/develop/development-builds/introduction](https://docs.expo.dev/develop/development-builds/introduction/)). EAS Update ships "non-native pieces (such as JS, styling, and images) over-the-air" so UI iteration skips rebuilds entirely ([docs.expo.dev/eas-update/introduction](https://docs.expo.dev/eas-update/introduction/); exact publish latency is not stated — gap). Free tier: 15 iOS + 15 Android builds/month, 1 concurrency, low priority, 45-min timeout; low-priority queue "will frequently grow to an hour or more" during North American business hours ([expo.dev/pricing](https://expo.dev/pricing), [expo/fyi eas-build-queues](https://github.com/expo/fyi/blob/main/eas-build-queues.md)). Starter $19/mo buys high priority ($45 build credit, then usage-based, 2-hour timeout).

**Buy vs rent.** Used/refurb Mac mini M2 8GB/256 is roughly **$349–429** (secondary market roundups — **unverified**; Apple's own refurb store showed **zero** Mac mini inventory on a live fetch of [apple.com/shop/refurbished/mac/mac-mini](https://www.apple.com/shop/refurbished/mac/mac-mini)). Break-even: **3–4 months** against MacinCloud dedicated, **~5 months** against Scaleway M1. Buying wins past one quarter of active development.

**Decision:** don't rent a Mac and don't buy one yet — on cost and setup friction, not on capability. EAS Build covers the whole pipeline; the only missing piece is *seeing the app*, and the arriving iPhone solves that at zero recurring cost, whereas a rented Mac is €75–125/mo indefinitely. Note honestly that a rented Mac + Simulator **is** rated full interactive iteration by the research, so this is a spend decision you can reverse in an afternoon: buy Scaleway hours at €0.11/hr (or €75/mo) or a ~$400 used mini if an iOS-only visual bug appears that you cannot reproduce on Android, or if the iPhone slips.

⚠️ Unanswered and load-bearing: **nobody verified whether a device farm can install an ad-hoc/dev-client `.ipa`** (UDID/provisioning constraints) rather than only a TestFlight/production build. If the iPhone slips, that question decides whether farms are a stopgap at all.

## 3. Monorepo: yes, `apps/mobile` goes in this repo

**Verdict: in-repo, keep the isolated linker.**

- Expo has first-class pnpm-workspace support, and **SDK 52+ auto-detects monorepos**: `watchFolders`, `resolver.nodeModulesPath`, and `resolver.disableHierarchicalLookup` "should be removed from manual metro.config.js configurations when migrating to SDK 52+… now handled automatically by `expo/metro-config`" ([docs.expo.dev/guides/monorepos](https://docs.expo.dev/guides/monorepos/), page dated June 30 2026). So the "actual recommended config" is **near-empty** — resist the stale-blog urge to hand-write resolver knobs.
- **The `node-linker=hoisted` question is now answered in your favour**: "Starting with SDK 54, Expo supports isolated dependencies… pnpm using this as the default installation strategy unless it's disabled." Hoisted is the *fallback* for specific RN libraries that break under isolation, not a blanket requirement. The mechanism is Metro's on-demand filesystem: "On-demand crawling allows symlinks to be resolved outside of your monorepo root, which adds Global Virtual Store support in package managers such as Bun and pnpm… enabled by default" ([docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/config/metro](https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/config/metro/)).
  - **Contradiction, stated openly:** Expo's own docs contain both eras. Pre-SDK 54 guidance says disable isolated installs "to avoid native build errors"; SDK 54+ says isolated is first-class. Every blog or gist dated before mid-2026 encodes the old constraint. Treat the isolated linker as *probably fine but trial-required*, not as proven for this dependency set.
- **The raw-TS `@gym/*` packages**: Metro resolves `package.json` `exports` maps by default since SDK 53 — `unstable_enablePackageExports` is on unless you turn it off ([docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/config/metro](https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/config/metro/)). Verified locally that `packages/domain/package.json` and `packages/ui/package.json` point straight at `./src/*.ts(x)` with no `main`/`module`/`types` and no build script — the exact shape Metro's default resolution targets. **Not verified:** whether Metro handles `@gym/ui`'s many deep nested subpaths (`./forge/agenda/session-view`) as cleanly as the single-entry examples in Expo's docs. Trial build required.
- **`server-only` is a hard crash, by design.** The package is a conditional-exports switch: `react-server` → `empty.js`, `default` → `index.js`, which is "a single error throw statement" ([nico.fyi/blog/server-only-package](https://www.nico.fyi/blog/server-only-package), marked *inferred*). Metro does not set the `react-server` condition, so any mobile file importing `@gym/data/server` throws at import time. That is the poison pill working — but it fails at runtime, so add the same `.dependency-cruiser.cjs` boundary rule (`apps/mobile` ✗→ `@gym/data/server`) that guards the rest of the repo, so it fails at `pnpm lint` instead.
- **Two integration chores nobody can skip.** (i) `pnpm-workspace.yaml` catalogs `react: 19.2.4` / `next: 16.2.6` "so they can never diverge into duplicate-React / hook breakage" — but RN pins React to its own release train, so `apps/mobile` must either join the catalog *at whatever version the SDK dictates* or explicitly opt out. (ii) `turbo.json`'s `build` task hardcodes `outputs: [".next/**"]`; a native app has no `.next`, and EAS Build — not `turbo run build` — produces the binary, so `apps/mobile` needs its own task key or exclusion.
- **EAS mechanics:** run all EAS CLI commands from `apps/mobile`, with `eas.json`/`credentials.json` there; the documented escape hatch for extra workspace setup is a `postinstall` that builds sibling packages ([docs.expo.dev/build-reference/build-with-monorepos](https://docs.expo.dev/build-reference/build-with-monorepos/)). `.easignore` at the monorepo root plus `EAS_NO_VCS=1` / `EAS_PROJECT_ROOT` is **unverified** — it rests on a dev.to post, not an Expo docs page.

⚠️ **Smoke-test before you commit to this plan.** `eas-cli` has an active bug history structurally identical to your setup: [#3247 "EAS Build fails to detect lock file and local monorepo packages in pnpm workspace"](https://github.com/expo/eas-cli/issues/3247) (symptom: "No lockfile found", plus fetching `workspace:*` packages from the npm registry and 404ing) and [#2978 "EAS mistakes pnpm for yarn workspace"](https://github.com/expo/eas-cli/issues/2978). #3247 shows Closed as of Nov 4 2025 but **no resolution was visible in the fetched body — "closed" is not evidence of "fixed"**. A throwaway `eas build` against a hello-world `apps/mobile` importing one `@gym/domain` symbol is a half-day that de-risks the whole architecture.

**SDK facts — all flagged unverified** (synthesized from search, not a fetched changelog): SDK **56** announced ~May 21 2026, RN 0.85, React 19.2; SDK 55 dropped Legacy Architecture entirely and removed `newArchEnabled` from app.json, so **New Architecture/Fabric is the only option**, not merely the default ([expo.dev/changelog/sdk-56](https://expo.dev/changelog/sdk-56)). Verify before pinning. Expo Router vs React Navigation was **not verified against a primary source** (subagent gap) — no sourced recommendation exists here.

## 5. Multi-tenancy without a hostname

**Decision: one neutral `iBookit` binary; resolve the tenant from the authenticated user's membership rows; gym-switcher for multi-gym staff; deep links and gym-code screens are pre-auth *hints* only, never the source of truth.** This mirrors web's `resolveTenant` with auth replacing the host header.

The store rules make the alternative dangerous:

- **4.2.6** (fetched live from [developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/)): "Apps created from a commercialized template or app generation service will be rejected **unless they are submitted directly by the provider of the app's content**… Another acceptable option for template providers is to create **a single binary to host all client content in an aggregated or 'picker' model**." The single-binary path is named as acceptable in Apple's own text.
- **4.3(a)**: "Don't create multiple Bundle IDs of the same app (for example, submitting a separate map app for every city in the world instead of a single worldwide map that allows users to search any city)." A per-gym-build strategy walks into this example.
- **Google Play** recommends per-client listings and (recommends, does not mandate) separate developer accounts for white-label strategies ("Each app – even if it is a branded template app – should have its own compelling store listing with a unique description, icons, graphics, and relevant screenshots", [support.google.com/…/answer/15884185](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/15884185?hl=en)) — but that guidance is written *for* the N-listings shape and no Play text was found barring a single multi-tenant app (inferred). Play's Repetitive Content policy text could only be obtained as **paraphrase, not verbatim — unverified** ([support.google.com/…/answer/9899034](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9899034)).

**What runtime theming buys and what it can't.** Brand token *values* are JS/JSON and ship OTA fine. But **icon, splash screen and app name are baked at build time** — configured via `icon`, `ios.icon`, `android.adaptiveIcon` and the `expo-splash-screen` plugin in app config, applied to the native project at build/prebuild ([docs.expo.dev/develop/user-interface/splash-screen-and-app-icon](https://docs.expo.dev/develop/user-interface/splash-screen-and-app-icon.md), modificationDate June 26 2026). iOS alternate app icons (`UIApplication.setAlternateIconName`, wrapped by `expo-alternate-app-icons`) let you switch between a **pre-bundled fixed set**, with iOS showing a system alert on change (inferred, from npm/GitHub summaries) — so it is a partial trick for a small closed roster, useless for an open-ended gym list. **The honest consequence: a white-label product on one binary means every gym's staff installs an app called iBookit with the iBookit icon and iBookit splash, and only sees their brand after launch.** That is a product/positioning decision to make now, not a technical detail.

Two escape hatches were **not** established: Apple Business Manager Custom Apps as a documented 4.2.6 remedy for a *public* listing is **unverified** (forum/blog anecdote only), and the 2017 TechCrunch claim that clients must hold their own developer accounts appears superseded by the current text, which centers on *who submits*, not who owns the account — also **unverified**. No real-world 2024–2026 4.2.6 rejection reports for multi-tenant SaaS surfaced; the verdict rests on guideline text, not precedent.

## 6. What replaces "push to main = deploy"

Nothing does, and that is the point.

| | Web (Vercel) | Mobile |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | `git push` to main (owner-gated) | `eas build` — a deliberate CLI act, decoupled from git |
| Gate | none | Apple/Play review (no primary-source SLA was obtained — the "90% in 24h" figures are search summaries, **unverified**) |
| Release | instant, atomic | manual, or Apple **phased release** (7-day 1/2/5/10/20/50/100%, pausable up to 30 days — *inferred*) / Play **staged rollout** (same ladder, "won't increase automatically… you need to manually increase it", *inferred* from [support.google.com/…/answer/6346149](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/6346149); updates only, not first publish) |
| Rollback | instant revert | none for a binary — pause the rollout, or ship a new build/OTA |

**The OTA rule, from the operative text.** Apple **2.5.2** (fetched live): apps "may not download, install, or execute code which introduces or changes features or functionality of the app". Google's **Device and Network Abuse** policy (fetched live, [support.google.com/…/answer/9888379](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9888379)): "an app may not download executable code (such as dex, JAR, .so files) from a source other than Google Play. **This restriction does not apply to code that runs in a virtual machine or an interpreter** where either provides indirect access to Android APIs". That interpreter carve-out is what EAS Update rides on. Apple's ADPLA §3.3.2 could **not** be re-verified — the PDF 404'd; the historical text is mirrored from a 2018 HN thread and a gist, so **cite 2.5.2, not §3.3.2**, and note that "JS-over-the-air is compliant" is Expo/community practice, **not an Apple carve-out naming RN** (inferred).

**OTA-able:** copy, JS logic fixes, new screens from existing components, brand token/theme values, new Supabase RPC calls from the existing client. **Needs a new binary:** any native module, an Expo SDK or RN bump, any new permission string, icon/splash changes ([docs.expo.dev/eas-update/introduction](https://docs.expo.dev/eas-update/introduction/)).

**Decisions:** use the **`fingerprint`** runtimeVersion policy — it "automatically increments whenever anything that may impact the native runtime changes, making incompatible updates extremely unlikely", where `appVersion` "requires manual discipline" ([docs.expo.dev/eas-update/runtime-versions](https://docs.expo.dev/eas-update/runtime-versions/)). Exactly two channels: `production` + `preview`. (EAS Update rollback-by-republish is **inferred** from the channels/branches model, not verified against a rollback doc.)

**New backend surface on the shared Supabase project:** a push-token table + RLS + register/unregister RPCs (S); FCM v1 service-account JSON and an APNs key, both generated through `eas credentials` (S–M, [docs.expo.dev/push-notifications/push-notifications-setup](https://docs.expo.dev/push-notifications/push-notifications-setup/)); an Edge Function calling the Expo Push API, mirroring the existing `send-email` pattern (S–M); optional device/session records. **The real new discipline is RPC versioning:** review latency plus a 7-day rollout plus users who never update means a shipped binary's call shapes stay live for weeks-to-months after main moves. Rule: **RPC changes additive and backward-compatible for at least one full release-and-rollout cycle** — never rename/remove a parameter or return column a shipped binary calls; add optional params with defaults or a `_v2` name and keep the old one alive. Key posture confirmed: publishable/anon key on device is fine, `service_role` never. Note Supabase's 2025 rename to `sb_publishable_`/`sb_secret_` with legacy JWT keys "deprecated by the end of 2026" — **which format this project currently issues was not checked**.

## 7. Alternatives — and a real tension in the findings

Subagent 7's ranking, which **does not match this brief's RN-rebuild premise**, stated rather than averaged:

- **(a) PWA-only: fails the goal outright on iOS.** No route lists a bare PWA on the App Store; it must be wrapped, and PWABuilder's own generated iOS project is "routinely rejected" under 4.2 without native functionality — and compiling it needs a Mac (*inferred*, [blog.pwabuilder.com](https://blog.pwabuilder.com/posts/publish-your-pwa-to-the-ios-app-store/), [pwa-builder/pwabuilder-ios-app-store](https://github.com/pwa-builder/pwabuilder-ios-app-store)). Android is fine via TWA/Bubblewrap with `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` matching the APK signing key ([developers.google.com/codelabs/pwa-in-play](https://developers.google.com/codelabs/pwa-in-play)). iOS web push works only for home-screen-installed PWAs, from iOS 16.4 **outside the EU**; Apple's EU home-screen-webapp removal in 17.4 was reversed 2024-03-01 ([techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2024/03/01/apple-reverses-decision-about-blocking-web-apps-on-iphones-in-the-eu/)). Safari's 7-day storage eviction applies to tabs, **not** standalone home-screen PWAs (*inferred*, [webkit.org/blog/14403](https://webkit.org/blog/14403/updates-to-storage-policy/)).
- **(b) Capacitor / webview wrapper: fastest to two listings, real iOS risk.** Guideline 4.2 verbatim: "Your app should include features, content, and UI that elevate it beyond a repackaged website. If your app is not particularly useful, unique, or app-like, it doesn't belong on the App Store." The "4.2 is the #1 wrapper rejection reason in 2025-26" claim is **unverified** — it traces entirely to vendor blogs and forum anecdotes, with **no Apple ruling, guideline revision, or published statistic found**. Mac-less Capacitor builds are claimed possible via Ionic Appflow / Xcode Cloud / Capawesome (*inferred*), but whether Xcode Cloud can do it **end-to-end without ever touching a Mac to configure the scheme is unresolved**.
- **(c) Expo shell + a few genuinely native screens (QR/camera check-in, push) + webview for the rest** — subagent 7's recommendation: satisfies 4.2 by construction, reuses the existing admin UI, and grows into (d).
- **(d) Full RN/Expo rebuild** — lowest long-term risk and maintenance cost, slowest to first listing. Its cost could not be quantified because the subagent-4 sizing never came back.

**Where the findings pull against each other:** subagent 7 recommends starting at (c); the brief and subagents 3/5/6 are all built around (d). They are reconcilable — (c) and (d) share the same Expo shell, EAS pipeline, monorepo config, tenancy model and backend surface, and differ only in how many screens are native on day one. But **you cannot rank (c) against (d) on time-to-listing without the rebuild sizing that is missing.** That is the single most decision-relevant gap in this report.

## 8. The plan — sequenced, and what each decision is

**Decide before writing code:**

| Decision | Recommendation | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Store shape | **One neutral iBookit binary**, runtime-themed | 4.2.6 single-binary safe harbor; 4.3(a) per-city example |
| Tenant resolution | **Auth first, then membership rows**; gym-switcher for multi-gym staff; deep links as hints only | mirrors web `resolveTenant`; no hostname exists |
| Repo | **`apps/mobile` inside this workspace**, isolated linker retained | SDK 54 isolated-first-class; SDK 52+ auto-config |
| Boundary | dependency-cruiser rule `apps/mobile` ✗→ `@gym/data/server` | `server-only` throws at import, a runtime failure you want at lint time |
| runtimeVersion | **`fingerprint`**, two channels | Expo's own "manual discipline" warning on `appVersion` |
| Keys | publishable on device; `service_role` never | Supabase api-keys doc |
| RPC changes | additive-only for one full rollout cycle | binaries age behind main |
| Data-access shape | **no recommendation — research missing** | subagent 4 null |
| Expo Router vs React Navigation | **no recommendation — not verified against a primary source** | subagent 3 gap |
| New Architecture | mandatory on SDK 55+ (**unverified**) | verify the changelog before pinning |

**Week 1, Windows only, no hardware:**
1. **Attempt Apple Developer Program enrollment in a Windows browser, today.** This is the fork in the road (individual vs org, and the identity-verification unknown). Everything else can proceed while it processes.
2. **Spike `apps/mobile`**: hello-world Expo app, one import from `@gym/domain`, then `eas build --platform android`. This tests the two things doc-reading cannot settle — the eas-cli pnpm-workspace bugs (#3247/#2978) and Metro's handling of `@gym/ui`'s deep subpath exports. If it fails, you learn now, not after building screens.
3. **Re-run the missing research** (data-access shape + Supabase Auth in Expo + rebuild sizing) before any data-layer or screen code exists.
4. Android is the full loop from day one — build, install, iterate, ship to Play. Do all UI work here.

**Week 2+, still no Apple hardware:** iOS builds and TestFlight *internal* setup are unblocked once enrollment clears — you can produce, sign, submit and configure an iOS build you cannot look at. Push credentials (APNs key via `eas credentials`) too. Do not queue external TestFlight yet; it needs Beta App Review.

**When the iPhone arrives:** the loop closes. Dev build + `expo-dev-client` + EAS Update gives you iOS UI iteration on a real device at no recurring cost. This — not a Mac — is the cheapest thing that unblocks iOS design work, and it is also what unblocks real App Store screenshots (whether compliant screenshots are obtainable with *no* device at all was **never investigated** — flagged as a gap).

**When/if a Mac arrives:** it adds local Xcode compiles, the Simulator, and cabled debugging. Nothing in the ship path above depends on it. **A Mac is genuinely never needed for:** enrollment, signing, building, submitting, TestFlight, App Store Connect, OTA updates, or push credentials.

## What would change this answer

1. **Enrollment demands an Apple device.** If [developer.apple.com/help/account/membership/identity-verification](https://developer.apple.com/help/account/membership/identity-verification/) turns out to gate *baseline individual enrollment* on Face ID/Touch ID or a T2 Mac, the entire iOS track slips to the iPhone's arrival. This is one direct fetch, or one enrollment attempt, away from settled.
2. **The EAS + pnpm-workspace spike fails.** If eas-cli still misdetects the workspace or can't resolve `workspace:*` packages, the fallbacks in order are: `node-linker=hoisted` (costs the dependency-boundary backstop), then a separate repo. A green spike build makes the in-repo verdict solid; a red one reopens question 3 entirely.
3. **The missing subagent-4 audit comes back saying the rebuild is enormous.** A large sizing flips the recommendation from a full RN rebuild toward subagent 7's hybrid (c) — shell + native check-in/push + webview for the long tail — as the first listing.
4. **Real 4.2.6 rejection precedent for multi-tenant SaaS surfaces.** The one-binary verdict rests on guideline text with zero corroborating rejection reports. Evidence that Apple treats a re-branded B2B platform as a template service would force a rethink toward per-client submissions under the "submitted directly by the provider of the app's content" clause.
5. **The white-label icon/splash constraint proves commercially unacceptable.** If gym clients require their own icon and name on the home screen, one binary is off the table regardless of what Apple permits, and the whole store strategy inverts.
6. **SDK 56 facts turn out wrong.** The SDK number, RN version, and New-Architecture-only claim were never fetched from a changelog. If the current SDK is older than 54, the isolated-linker verdict reverts to "hoisted required" and the monorepo cost calculus changes.
7. **The iPhone slips.** Then the only substitute is a browser device farm — and whether a farm can install an ad-hoc/dev-client `.ipa` at all is unverified. Answer that before betting on it; otherwise the fallback is a rented Mac (Scaleway €0.11/hr, MacStadium $109/mo) which the findings *do* rate as full interactive iteration.

## Run metadata

- Question: What is the fastest, lowest-risk route to ship the RED-2.0 **admin** app as a single React Native + Expo app on both the iOS App Store and Google Play, starting development TODAY with NO Mac and NO iPhone (Android hardware fully available; an iPhone arrives first, a Mac later or possibly never)? Cover, with sourced evidence and concrete decisions:

(1) MAC-LESS iOS PATH — end to end. Exactly which steps of the iOS lifecycle can be done with zero Apple hardware: Apple Developer Program enrollment (individual vs organization, D-U-N-S, cost, how long approval takes, can it be completed from a Windows browser or does it need the Apple Developer iOS app?), EAS Build cloud macOS workers, EAS-managed credentials (certs/provisioning profiles generated without Keychain), EAS Submit to App Store Connect, TestFlight internal/external testing, App Store Connect from a browser. What is IMPOSSIBLE without a Mac? What is impossible without an *iPhone*? Be explicit about the difference — a lot of guidance conflates them. Include Expo Go vs development builds vs internal distribution, and how you iterate on iOS UI when your only feedback loop is a cloud build + a physical iPhone (build turnaround, EAS Update / OTA to skip rebuilds, `expo-dev-client`).

(2) SIMULATOR / RENTAL ALTERNATIVES — rank them on cost, setup friction, and how well they actually substitute for a local Mac: EAS Build's `--profile` simulator builds, MacinCloud, MacStadium, AWS EC2 Mac (note the 24h minimum allocation), Scaleway/Hetzner Mac minis, GitHub Actions macOS runners, Codemagic, and browser-based device farms (BrowserStack App Live, LambdaTest, Sauce Labs, AWS Device Farm) for running an .ipa on a real remote iPhone. Which of these lets us do *interactive UI iteration* vs only *verification*? Give real 2026 pricing where you can source it. Also: is buying a cheap used Mac mini M1/M2 simply cheaper than 6 months of rental?

(3) MONOREPO INTEGRATION — the big one. Can `apps/mobile` (Expo) live inside this existing **pnpm 11 + Turborepo** workspace alongside the two Next.js apps, or does it need its own repo? Specifically: Metro bundler + pnpm's **isolated/symlinked** node_modules (this repo relies on pnpm's isolated linker as a dependency-boundary backstop — see constraints), `expo/metro-config` monorepo settings (`watchFolders`, `nodeModulesPaths`, `disableHierarchicalLookup`), whether `node-linker=hoisted` is required and what that would cost this repo, Metro symlink support status in 2026, and how the JIT raw-TypeScript `@gym/*` packages (no build step, consumed via Next `transpilePackages`) behave under Metro. Does Metro transpile workspace TS source the way Next does? What breaks? Give the *actual* recommended config. Also cover Turborepo task wiring for EAS Build (EAS builds run on a cloud worker that must install the whole monorepo — `eas.json` `cli.requireCommit`, `.easignore`, workspace root detection, pnpm version pinning).

(4) CODE REUSE — how much of this app actually transfers, honestly. The admin app is React Server Components + server actions + a `server-only` Supabase DAL + a Tailwind-v4 DOM component kit. None of RSC/server-actions/DOM exists in React Native. So: which layers reuse as-is (pure TS domain rules, formatters, generated DB types), which must be rebuilt (every screen, every primitive), and what the realistic rebuild size is for 9 routes / ~80 admin files / 44 UI-kit files. Evaluate the two data-access shapes for RN: (a) device talks to Supabase directly with `@supabase/supabase-js` + RLS + `AsyncStorage`/`expo-secure-store` session persistence, vs (b) the mobile app calls a new HTTP API surface on the existing Next app (route handlers) so the existing server DAL and its RLS/tenant logic stay the single source of truth. Which preserves this repo's server-seam architecture, and what does each cost? Cover Supabase Auth in Expo concretely: session persistence, `autoRefreshToken` + AppState, deep links / `expo-linking` for magic-link and email-confirmation flows, and PKCE.

(5) MULTI-TENANCY WITHOUT A HOST HEADER — the architectural crux. Web resolves tenant from the **hostname** (`gym_domain` row → `x-gym` slug + `x-brand` brand-module key, stamped in `proxy.ts`, brand tokens SSR-inlined for no FOUC). A native app has no hostname and one binary serves every gym. Enumerate and rank the options: resolve tenant from the authenticated user's membership rows at login; a gym-code / slug entry screen; per-gym white-label builds (multiple App Store listings) vs one neutral `iBookit` listing that themes at runtime; deep-link/universal-link seeding. Include Apple's and Google's rules on **white-label / template / one-app-per-client** submissions (App Store Review Guideline 4.2.6 and 4.3, and Google Play's equivalent) — this repo is a multi-tenant platform re-branded per gym client, so a per-gym-build strategy may be rejected outright. What does the runtime-theming path require (brand tokens shipped in the binary vs fetched, splash/icon are per-binary and CANNOT be themed at runtime — what does that mean for a white-label product?).

(6) HOSTING & DEPLOY MODEL — does mobile 'host' like the Vercel apps do? Explain plainly what replaces Vercel: EAS Build/Submit/Update, app store review cycles, the fact that there is no 'push to main = deploy' for the binary, what EAS Update *can* ship OTA and what it legally/technically cannot (Apple 3.3.2 / Play policy on code push), version/runtime-version management, and how mobile releases interleave with this repo's push-to-main-deploys-Vercel workflow. The Supabase database is shared and unchanged — confirm what that implies (same RLS, same RPCs, anon key on device is fine, service-role key is NOT) and what new DB/edge-function surface a mobile client forces (push tokens, device sessions, API versioning as the binary in the wild ages behind main).

(7) ALTERNATIVES TO A FULL RN REWRITE — evaluate seriously, don't strawman: (a) PWA-only / installable web app — what does that actually get on iOS in 2026 (push, standalone, home-screen install) and does it satisfy the goal of 'be in both marketplaces'? (b) Capacitor or a `react-native-webview` shell wrapping the existing Next admin app — the fastest possible route to two store listings; evaluate the App Store Review 4.2 'minimum functionality' rejection risk for a wrapped web app in 2026 with real recent evidence, and what native capability (push, camera/QR scanning for check-in, offline, biometrics) would have to be added to survive review. (c) Expo + selective native screens with the rest in a webview. (d) Full native RN rebuild. Rank these on time-to-first-store-listing, rejection risk, long-term maintenance cost against a 2-app monorepo, and how well each works with the no-Mac constraint.

(8) THE ACTUAL RECOMMENDED PLAN — a sequenced, dated-by-week route we can start on today on Windows+Android hardware, naming what to build first, what is unblocked by the iPhone arriving, what is unblocked (or not) by a Mac arriving, and where a Mac is genuinely never needed. Call out the decisions that must be made before writing code (tenant resolution, data-access shape, one listing vs many, Expo Router vs React Navigation, New Architecture/Fabric status in the current Expo SDK) and give a recommendation for each, not a menu.

Ground every claim in primary sources: Expo/EAS docs, Apple App Store Review Guidelines + App Store Connect docs, Google Play policy, Supabase docs, Metro/pnpm/Turborepo docs. Flag anything that changed recently or where sources disagree — this ecosystem moves fast and stale blog posts are the main failure mode here.
